# KyPhone phone checklist

*Generated by `spi_bridge/tools/make_phone_checklist.py` from `tests/test_navigation.py`; never edit by hand.*

Part 1 is what only the real phone can show. Part 2 is the navigation the tests already check in the emulator, for a run-through on the phone after a big change. The test phone has three contacts (Ann Lee, Pip Okonkwo, Zed with no number), a conversation with Ann and one with a number not in contacts, a book, an album, a note and a call; on the real phone, use your own.

## Part 1: only on the phone

### The panel

- [ ] Wake the phone and open every home menu item. **Expect:** Every screen is drawn whole: no missing rows, no garbage, nothing cut mid-word.
- [ ] Scroll a long list (texts, contacts) up and down. **Expect:** Partial refreshes only, no flashing while scrolling; a full refresh moving between home and an app.
- [ ] Leave a screen up for a minute, then move. **Expect:** No ghosting left behind after the next full refresh.
- [ ] Open a book and turn ten pages. **Expect:** Every page arrives complete; the footer shows the chapter, page and %.
- [ ] Receive a text with an emoji. **Expect:** The emoji is drawn as a picture in the bubble and the texts list.

### Speed (the timing line on the serial log)

- [ ] Move one row on the home menu. **Expect:** About half a second; the log shows total near 465 ms for a partial frame.
- [ ] Open an app. **Expect:** About 1.3 s for its full refresh.

### Keyboard and trackpad

- [ ] Type a sentence in a note. **Expect:** Every letter appears; Q, W, A, S, D type letters.
- [ ] Swipe the trackpad in all four directions, in both trackpad modes. **Expect:** Each moves the selection the right way (left is left).
- [ ] Press the coloured buttons: circle, triangle, cross. **Expect:** Circle: lock, then home; triangle: up a level; cross: lock, then back where you were.
- [ ] Leave the phone alone for 30 s on the home menu. **Expect:** It locks itself; any key returns to the home menu.

### Screen light

- [ ] Settings > Screen light, step it up and down. **Expect:** The light follows each step, 0 to 8.
- [ ] Leave it for 5 s. **Expect:** The light goes off; the next key turns it back on.

### Texting (the modem; sends use the plan allowance, so a handful only)

- [ ] Look at the home menu. **Expect:** Signal bars match the reception (not a fixed three).
- [ ] Send a text to your own phone. **Expect:** SENDING... then SENT; it arrives.
- [ ] Reply from your own phone, including a long text and an emoji. **Expect:** It arrives in the same conversation, joined, with the emoji.
- [ ] Take the SIM out (or go out of signal) and send. **Expect:** NOT SENT; Enter on it retries once signal is back.
- [ ] Power the phone off and on, then text it. **Expect:** Texting works without a restart (the modem is retried every 10 s).

### Music (the headphone output)

- [ ] Play an album with headphones in. **Expect:** Sound in both ears; Up/Down change the volume.
- [ ] Leave now playing, go home. **Expect:** The music goes on; the equalizer mark shows by LISTEN.
- [ ] Restart the phone, open LISTEN. **Expect:** RESUME leads the list and starts where it stopped.

### Wi-Fi and Bluetooth (the real radios)

- [ ] Settings > Wi-Fi, join a network with a wrong then a right password. **Expect:** COULDNT CONNECT, then CONNECTED; Settings shows it joined.
- [ ] Settings > Bluetooth, PAIR NEW DEVICE with headphones. **Expect:** They pair and connect.
- [ ] Try to switch Bluetooth off. **Expect:** Refused while the keyboard is connected.

### Add from a computer

- [ ] Settings > Add from a computer, open the address on a laptop. **Expect:** The page asks for the six-digit code shown on the phone.
- [ ] Drop a book, a song and a .vcf. **Expect:** Each is listed on the phone; the book, album and contacts appear in their apps.

## Part 2: navigation, screen by screen (207 checks)

### Lock and home

**From the lock screen (locked from home):**

- [ ] Down: Locked by hand (Esc on home): any key opens the home menu, on TEXT.

**From the home menu:**

- [ ] Esc: Esc on the home menu locks the phone.
- [ ] q: Q on the home menu locks the phone.
- [ ] Up: Up on TEXT stays on TEXT (the status bar is never selected).
- [ ] Down x9: Down stops at SETTINGS, the last row.
- [ ] Right, Left: Right and Left move like Down and Up.
- [ ] Down, Enter: Enter on CALL opens the call list.
- [ ] Down x2, Enter: Enter on READ opens the books.
- [ ] Down x3, Enter: Enter on LISTEN opens the albums.
- [ ] Down x4, Enter: Enter on CONTACTS opens the address book.
- [ ] Down x5, Enter: Enter on NOTES opens the notes.
- [ ] Down x6, Enter: Enter on SETTINGS opens Settings.
- [ ] Enter: Enter on TEXT opens the texts.

**From an incoming call (i on home):**

- [ ] Esc: Esc on an incoming call: missed, logged as MISS.
- [ ] Enter: Enter answers.
- [ ] Enter, Esc: Hanging up an answered call logs it as IN.

### Texts

**From the texts:**

- [ ] Esc: Esc on the texts goes home, still on TEXT.
- [ ] q: Q on the texts goes home.
- [ ] Backspace: Backspace on the texts goes home.
- [ ] Enter: Enter on a conversation opens it.
- [ ] +: The + key opens New Message.
- [ ] Up: Up from the first conversation selects the header back <.
- [ ] Up, Enter: Enter on the header < goes home.
- [ ] Up, Right, Enter: Enter on the header + opens New Message.
- [ ] Up, Down: Down from the header returns to the first conversation.
- [ ] Down x5: Down stops at the last conversation.

**From Ann's conversation:**

- [ ] Esc: Esc in a conversation goes back to the texts.
- [ ] q: Q in a conversation is a letter: it types q.
- [ ] Up: Up from the composer selects the newest message.
- [ ] Up x2: Up from the oldest message selects the header back <.
- [ ] Up, Right: Right from a selected message jumps to the header info i.
- [ ] Up, Left: Left from a selected message jumps to the header back <.
- [ ] Up x2, Enter: Enter on the header < goes back to the texts.
- [ ] Up, Right, Enter: Enter on the header i opens the person.
- [ ] Up x2, Down x2: Down from the header walks back down to the composer.
- [ ] Up, Enter: Enter on a selected message opens it full screen.
- [ ] Up, h: Typing with a message selected returns to the composer and types.
- [ ] Enter: Enter with nothing typed says there is nothing to send.

**From a stranger's conversation:**

- [ ] Up, Right, Enter: A stranger's conversation: i opens their number as NOT IN CONTACTS.
- [ ] Esc: Esc in a stranger's conversation goes back to the texts.

**From a message opened full screen:**

- [ ] Esc: Esc on a full-screen message returns with that message still selected.
- [ ] Enter: Enter on a full-screen message returns to the conversation.
- [ ] Backspace: Backspace on a full-screen message returns to the conversation.
- [ ] Down: Down on a one-page message stays (it redraws).

**From the nothing-to-send alert:**

- [ ] Enter: Enter on that alert returns to the conversation.
- [ ] Esc: Esc on that alert returns to the conversation too.

**From New Message:**

- [ ] Esc: Esc on an empty New Message goes back to the texts without asking.
- [ ] Up: Up from TO selects the header X.
- [ ] Up, Down: Down from the X returns to TO.
- [ ] Up, Enter: Enter on the X of an empty message leaves.
- [ ] Enter: Enter on an empty TO opens the contact picker.
- [ ] Right, Enter: Right from an empty TO selects +, Enter opens the picker.
- [ ] Right, Left: Left from + returns to TO.
- [ ] q: Q in New Message is a letter.
- [ ] type 5550100101, Enter: Enter on a filled TO moves to MESSAGE.
- [ ] type 5550100101, Enter, Up: Up from MESSAGE returns to TO.
- [ ] type 5550100101, Enter, Down, Up: Down to SEND, Up back to MESSAGE.
- [ ] type 5550100101, Enter x2: Enter on an empty MESSAGE says there is nothing to send.
- [ ] Tab, h, Enter: Sending with no TO says there is no one to send to.
- [ ] 1, 2, Tab, h, Enter x2: A number that cannot be texted: after the alert the cursor is back on TO, the message kept.
- [ ] type 5550100101, Enter, h, Enter: Enter on a written message sends it.
- [ ] 5, Esc: Esc with something typed asks before discarding.

**From Discard this message?:**

- [ ] Esc: Esc on Discard? keeps editing, nothing lost.
- [ ] Enter: Enter on KEEP EDITING keeps editing.
- [ ] Left, Right, Enter: Left then Right returns to the safe button.
- [ ] Left, Enter: Left, Enter on DISCARD throws it away.

### Contacts

**From the address book:**

- [ ] Esc: Esc on the address book goes home, on CONTACTS.
- [ ] q: Q in the address book is a letter (it searches).
- [ ] Up: Up from the first contact selects the header back <.
- [ ] Up, Enter: Enter on the header < goes home.
- [ ] Up, Right, Enter: Enter on the header + starts a new contact.
- [ ] +: The + key with nothing typed starts a new contact.
- [ ] p, +: With letters typed, + is just a character.
- [ ] p, Enter: Typing filters by name; Enter opens the match.
- [ ] z, z, Backspace x2: Backspace clears the search.
- [ ] Down x9: Down stops at the last contact.

**From Ann's page:**

- [ ] Esc: Esc on a person goes back to the address book.
- [ ] (as it opens): A saved person opens on CALL.
- [ ] Up, Enter: Up selects < ; Enter goes back.
- [ ] Up, Right, Enter: Up, Right selects EDIT; Enter opens the form.
- [ ] Enter: Enter on CALL calls them.
- [ ] Right, Enter: TEXT opens the conversation with them.
- [ ] Right x2: Right stops at TEXT.

**From the page of a contact with no number:**

- [ ] (as it opens): A person with no number opens on ADD NUMBER.
- [ ] Enter: Enter on ADD NUMBER opens the form.

**From a stranger's page:**

- [ ] Esc: Esc on an unsaved number goes back to its conversation.
- [ ] Down: Down from CALL reaches CREATE CONTACT.
- [ ] Down, Up: Up from CREATE CONTACT returns to CALL.
- [ ] Right x2: Right steps CALL, TEXT, CREATE CONTACT.
- [ ] Down, Enter: CREATE CONTACT opens the form with the number filled in and locked.

**From Ann's edit form:**

- [ ] Esc: Esc on the form goes back without saving.
- [ ] q: Q on the form is a letter.
- [ ] Up, Enter: Up from FIRST selects the header X; Enter leaves.
- [ ] Down x6: Down stops at SAVE.
- [ ] Down x3, Left, Right: Left from SAVE reaches DELETE, Right returns.
- [ ] Backspace x3, Down x3, Enter: SAVE with no first name says one is needed.
- [ ] Backspace x3, Down x3, Enter x2: After that alert, FIRST is selected.
- [ ] Down x2, Backspace x14, type 5550100101, Down, Enter: A number already saved is refused, naming who has it.
- [ ] Down x2, x: Letters cannot be typed into the number.

**From Delete contact?:**

- [ ] (as it opens): DELETE asks first, on KEEP CONTACT.
- [ ] Esc: Esc keeps the contact.
- [ ] Enter: Enter on KEEP CONTACT keeps it.
- [ ] Left, Enter: Left, Enter on DELETE removes it.

### Calls

**From the call list:**

- [ ] Esc: Esc on the call list goes home, on CALL.
- [ ] Backspace: Backspace on the call list goes home.
- [ ] Enter: Enter on DIAL A NUMBER opens the dialer.
- [ ] Down, Enter: Enter on a logged call opens that person's page.
- [ ] Down, Enter, Esc: Esc from that page returns to the call list.
- [ ] Up, Enter: Up to the header, Enter goes home.
- [ ] Down x5: Down stops at the last call.

**From the dialer:**

- [ ] Esc: Esc on the dialer goes back to the call list.
- [ ] Enter: Enter with nothing dialed does nothing.
- [ ] x, 5: Only digits, # and * can be dialed.
- [ ] Down, Enter: Down selects a quick-dial contact; Enter calls them.

**From a call ringing out:**

- [ ] Esc: Esc while ringing cancels; the call is logged with no length.
- [ ] Enter: (demo) Enter while ringing: they answer.
- [ ] circle, cross, Down: The coloured buttons do nothing during a call.

**From a call in progress:**

- [ ] Esc: Esc hangs up; the call is logged with its length.
- [ ] Down, Enter, q: Q hangs up too; other keys do nothing.

### Books

**From the books:**

- [ ] Esc: Esc on the books goes home, on READ.
- [ ] Enter: Enter opens a book.
- [ ] Up, Enter: Up to the header, Enter goes home.

**From a book:**

- [ ] Esc: Esc in a book goes back to the books, on that book.
- [ ] q: Q in a book goes back to the books.
- [ ] c: C opens the chapters.
- [ ] Left: Back on the first page says it is the first page.
- [ ] Left, Enter: Enter on that alert returns to the page.
- [ ] +, +, +: Bigger past the largest size says so.
- [ ] -, -: Smaller past the smallest size says so.

**From the chapters:**

- [ ] Esc: Esc on the chapters returns to the same page.
- [ ] (as it opens): The chapter being read is selected (HERE).
- [ ] Up, Enter: Up to the header, Enter returns to the page.
- [ ] Down, Enter: Enter on a chapter jumps to its start.
- [ ] Down x9: Down stops at the last chapter.

### Music

**From the albums:**

- [ ] Esc: Esc on the albums goes home, on LISTEN.
- [ ] Enter: Enter opens an album.
- [ ] Up, Enter: Up to the header, Enter goes home.

**From an album:**

- [ ] Esc: Esc on an album goes back to the albums.
- [ ] Up, Enter: Up to the header, Enter goes back to the albums.
- [ ] Down, Enter: Enter plays the album from that track.
- [ ] Down x9: Down stops at the last track.

**From now playing:**

- [ ] Esc: Esc on now playing goes back to the album; the music goes on.
- [ ] Esc x2, Enter: NOW PLAYING leads the albums; Enter shows it.
- [ ] Esc x2, Enter, Esc: Opened from the albums, Esc on now playing goes back to the albums.
- [ ] Enter: Enter pauses.
- [ ] Right: Right plays the next track.
- [ ] Right x4: Right at the last track redraws and stays.

### Notes

**From the notes:**

- [ ] Esc: Esc on the notes goes home, on NOTES.
- [ ] Enter: Enter opens a note.
- [ ] +: The + key starts a new note.
- [ ] Up, Enter: Up to the header <, Enter goes home.
- [ ] Up, Right, Enter: Header +, Enter starts a new note.

**From a note:**

- [ ] Esc: Esc on a note saves it and goes back.
- [ ] q: Q in a note is a letter.
- [ ] Enter: Enter starts a new line.
- [ ] Up: Up selects SAVE in the header.
- [ ] Up, Left, Enter: Left to <, Enter saves and goes back.
- [ ] Up, Enter: Enter on SAVE saves and goes back.

**From Delete note?:**

- [ ] (as it opens): DELETE asks first, on KEEP NOTE.
- [ ] Esc: Esc keeps the note.
- [ ] Left, Enter: Left, Enter on DELETE removes it.

### Settings

**From Settings:**

- [ ] Esc: Esc on Settings goes home, on SETTINGS.
- [ ] Up, Enter: Up to the header, Enter goes home.
- [ ] Down x9: Down stops at Add from a computer.
- [ ] Enter: Enter on Wi-Fi opens the Wi-Fi list.
- [ ] Down, Enter: Enter on Bluetooth opens the Bluetooth list.
- [ ] Down x3, Enter: Enter on Activity mark switches it, in place.

**From Screen light:**

- [ ] Esc: Esc on Screen light returns to Settings, on Screen light.
- [ ] Enter: Enter on Screen light is done.
- [ ] Right x12: Brighter stops at 8.
- [ ] Left x12: Dimmer stops at off.

**From Add from a computer:**

- [ ] Esc: Esc on Add from a computer stops the page.
- [ ] q: Q on Add from a computer stops the page.
- [ ] Enter: Enter on Add from a computer stops the page.

**From the Wi-Fi list:**

- [ ] (as it opens): The Wi-Fi list opens on the joined network.
- [ ] Esc: Esc on Wi-Fi goes back to Settings.
- [ ] Up x2, Enter: Up past the switch to the header, Enter goes back.
- [ ] Down: Down skips the OTHER NETWORKS label.
- [ ] Down, Up: Up skips the label too.

**From Forget network?:**

**From the Wi-Fi password box:**

- [ ] Up, Enter: Up selects <, Enter goes back without connecting.

- [ ] q: Q in the password box is a letter.

- [ ] type hunter22, Enter x2: Enter on CONNECTED shows the Wi-Fi list, joined.

**From a failed connection:**

- [ ] (as it opens): A wrong password says it could not connect.

**From the Bluetooth list:**

- [ ] Esc: Esc on Bluetooth goes back to Settings.
- [ ] Enter: Switching Bluetooth off while the keyboard uses it is refused.
- [ ] Enter x2: Enter on that alert returns to the Bluetooth list.
- [ ] down to Keyboard, Enter, Left, Enter: FORGET on the keyboard is refused.

**From a paired device (Forget / Re-connect):**

- [ ] (as it opens): Enter on a paired device asks, RE-CONNECT selected.
- [ ] Esc: Esc goes back to the Bluetooth list.
- [ ] Enter: Enter on RE-CONNECT connects.
- [ ] Enter x2: Enter on CONNECTED returns to the Bluetooth list.
- [ ] Left, Enter: Left, Enter on FORGET forgets it.

**From OTHER DEVICES:**

- [ ] Esc: Esc on OTHER DEVICES goes back to the Bluetooth list.
- [ ] q: Q on OTHER DEVICES goes back too.
- [ ] Enter: Enter on a new device pairs it.
- [ ] Enter x2: Enter on CONNECTED returns to the Bluetooth list.
